narrative: Five years in, full-year 2023 net income set a further record at $49.6 billion, absorbing a $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment tied to that year's bank failures, with First Republic contributing to results.

checks.a1: Supported across the window. Full-year net income set records in 2019, 2021 and 2023, with the pandemic year as the only dip. The December 2018 quarter did not mark a lasting credit-cycle turn.
checks.a2: Supported over the window, after a detour. Net income reached a record $49.6 billion in 2023 following the rate-driven 2022 gain, but the path went through a near-zero-rate dip first. Rates alone do not explain every year.
checks.a3: Supported. The bank acquired a seized regional bank's assets and deposits from the FDIC, a direct instance of scale and capital being used to take share. Integration costs are not yet known.
checks.a4: Not supported over the five years. Profit set records in three of five years, with provisioning rises in 2020 and 2022 each followed by renewed income growth rather than a lasting peak. A later downturn is not ruled out.
checks.a5: Choosing not to take a position is consistent with uncertainty. This outcome alone cannot tell us whether that was the better decision.

assumptions.text: The December quarter was market noise, not the credit cycle turning.
Higher rates will keep lifting net interest income.
Scale and capital will let the bank take share through the next downturn.
Rising provisions and expenses mark the top of the earnings cycle.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.
